subject: arts-music
essential_question: How can understanding curating, portfolio, and exhibition help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
project_brief: Curate a cross-arts portfolio or exhibition with contextual labels and process evidence. This is the grade 7 culminating project for "Curating, Portfolio, and Exhibition" (ma-g7-arts-and-music-u06, unit 6), built around curatorial theme, selection and sequencing, artist statements, audience experience, and feedback and revision. Curate a cross-arts portfolio or exhibition with contextual labels and process evidence. Choose whether the finished portfolio is shared privately with your facilitator, in writing only, or with a wider audience — the choice is yours and does not affect the score.
requirements: Address every topic listed for this unit: curatorial theme, selection and sequencing, artist statements, audience experience, feedback and revision, and reflection and future goals.
Meet the performance task as written: Curate a cross-arts portfolio or exhibition with contextual labels and process evidence.
Show your work or process, not just a final result — a process note, sketch log, commit history, or draft trail.
Complete the checklist in this package before submitting.
primary_task: Curate a cross-arts portfolio or exhibition with contextual labels and process evidence. Choose whether the finished portfolio is shared privately with your facilitator, in writing only, or with a wider audience — the choice is yours and does not affect the score.
critique_criteria: A named viewer, listener, or reader can point to a specific choice in the work and connect it back to curatorial theme or another named topic from this unit.
The piece shows at least one deliberate revision — a version-two decision made because the first attempt did not achieve the intended effect.
The student can explain the intended effect on an audience in their own words, separate from just describing what was made.
Only the student's own original work, public-domain material, or a properly licensed and cited excerpt appears in the piece — no unlicensed lyrics, sheet music, or protected work is reproduced.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: Sharing this project publicly is always optional and never required for full credit. You may present live to a small audience of your choosing, present privately to just your facilitator, submit a recording made only for your own review, or submit a written/described account of the finished work instead.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: If any part of this task could involve singing, speaking on camera, or being recorded, you may instead notate the piece, write a detailed description or script, use body percussion or an instrument in place of your voice, or perform live for your facilitator with no recording made at all. No lesson in this unit requires a voice recording, a camera, or a photo.

copyright_and_authorship: The final submitted work must remain your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI assistant may help you plan, explain a concept, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but may not produce the graded work itself. Use only your own original work, public-domain material, or a properly licensed and cited excerpt — never reproduce full copyrighted lyrics, sheet music, or another protected work without the rights to do so.
remediation: If the piece isn't coming together, return to a single, smaller exercise focused only on curatorial theme, revisit one worked example or model from this unit, and rebuild your confidence with that one element before returning to the full project.
extension: Once the core piece is finished, create a second short variation that explores selection and sequencing from a different angle, or write a short artist's statement comparing your original intent with what the finished work actually communicates.
